lines.text: Where does your breath go? Not into a bag. Into these.
lines.phonemes: wˌeə dˈʌz jɔː bɹˈɛθ ɡˈəʊ? nˌɒt ˌɪntʊ ɐ bˈaɡ. ˌɪntʊ ðˈiːz.

lines.text: Below your windpipe, the airways fork, again and again, up to about twenty-three times. At the tips hang about half a billion sacs. Each is about a fifth of a millimetre.
lines.phonemes: bɪlˌəʊ jɔː wˈɪndpaɪp, ðɪ ˈeəweɪz fˈɔːk, ɐɡˈɛn and ɐɡˈɛn, ˌʌp tʊ ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛntiθɹˈiː tˈaɪmz. at ðə tˈɪps hˈaŋ ɐbˌaʊt hˈɑːf ɐ bˈɪliən sˈaks. ˈiːtʃ ɪz ɐbˌaʊt ɐ fˈɪfθ əvə mˈɪlɪmˌiːtə.

lines.text: For centuries, physicians taught the lung was clotted blood, there to cool the heart. In sixteen sixty-one, Marcello Malpighi put an animal's lung under a microscope: bubbles.
lines.phonemes: fɔː sˈɛntʃəɹiz, fɪzˈɪʃənz tˈɔːt ðə lˈʌŋ wɒz klˈɒtɪd blˈʌd, ðeə tə kˈuːl ðə hˈɑːt. ɪn sˈɪkstiːn sˈɪkstiwˌɒn, mɑːtʃˈɛləʊ malpˈiːɡi pˌʊt ɐn ˈanɪməlz lˈʌŋ ˌʌndəɹ ɐ mˈaɪkɹəskˌəʊp: bˈʌbəlz.

lines.text: Each sac is wrapped in capillaries. Over much of it, the wall between air and blood is under half a micrometre: far thinner than a red cell. Oxygen slips across, no pump needed. Thicken that wall, and breathing gets harder.
lines.phonemes: ˈiːtʃ sˈak ɪz ɹˈapt ɪn kˈapɪləɹiz. ˌəʊvə mˈʌtʃ ɒv ɪt, ðə wˈɔːl bɪtwˌiːn ˈeə and blˈʌd ɪz ˌʌndə hˈɑːf ɐ mˈaɪkɹəʊmˌiːtə: fˈɑː θˈɪnə ðˌanə ɹˈɛd sˈɛl. ˈɒksɪdʒən slˈɪps əkɹˈɒs, nˈəʊ pˈʌmp nˈiːdɪd. θˈɪkən ðat wˈɔːl, and bɹˈiːðɪŋ ɡˈɛts hˈɑːdə.

lines.text: Unfold every sac flat, and they'd cover about seventy square metres. About a quarter of a tennis court, folded inside your chest.
lines.phonemes: ʌnfˈəʊld ˈɛvɹɪ sˈak flˈat, and ðeɪd kˈʌvəɹ ɐbˌaʊt sˈɛvənti skwˈeə mˈiːtəz. ɐbˌaʊt ɐ kwˈɔːtəɹ əvə tˈɛnɪs kˈɔːt, fˈəʊldɪd ɪnsˈaɪd jɔː tʃˈɛst.

lines.text: So your lungs aren't a bag. They're a sponge that spreads air thin.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ jɔː lˈʌŋz ˌɑːnt ɐ bˈaɡ. ðeɪəɹ ɐ spˈʌndʒ ðat spɹˈɛdz ˈeə θˈɪn.

lines.text: Meanwhile, as you watched, air went in and out of you. About six litres of it.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːnwaɪl, az juː wˈɒtʃt, ˈeə wˈɛnt ɪn and ˌaʊtəv juː. ɐbˌaʊt sˈɪks lˈiːtəz ɒv ɪt.

lines.text: Next: a cell that leaves your blood. It squeezes through a wall.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ɐ sˈɛl ðat lˈiːvz jɔː blˈʌd. ɪt skwˈiːzɪz θɹuː ɐ wˈɔːl.
